Two copies of the same event
A coding agent is looking for files that changed with reader dot py. Eight past commits contain it. Evict one copy of event thirteen. The second copy still provides its address.
Evict the last copy. The reader records thirteen as an exception. Seven resident addresses and one exception now identify all eight commits.
Recover more than one missing address
Drop event forty-five as well. The exception list now contains two addresses. Its union with the six remaining events still covers the complete history.
Query the file. The reader fetches just the two missing commit bodies. It skips the posting request. The leading test file changed alongside the anchor five times.
Switch off notifications and lose the same two events. Six addresses remain, and the reader can no longer identify the missing pair from its stored evidence.
Ask again. The reader requests the complete posting and fetches two bodies. The four ranked files and their scores exactly match the previous answer.
On six new repositories, four hundred eighty-five queries return identical rankings. At one kibibyte, maintaining exceptions transfers nine thousand two hundred thirteen bytes of SQLite payload.
At four kibibytes, the compressed complete list also fits often enough. It ties maintained exceptions at four thousand three hundred twenty-two bytes.
